title: Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (experimental v1)
description: Clinician-administered assessment of suicidal ideation and behavior. Ideation severity is the highest endorsed level 0-5; intensity, behavior, and lethality are recorded separately with no composite score.

items.prompt: Ideation 1 (Wish to be dead, recent): Have you wished you were dead, or wished you could go to sleep and not wake up?
Ideation 2 (Nonspecific active thoughts, recent): Have you had thoughts of killing yourself, without thinking about a method, intent, or plan?
Ideation 3 (Method, without intent, recent): Have you thought about how you might kill yourself, without intending to act on those thoughts?
Ideation 4 (Some intent, no specific plan, recent): Have you had suicidal thoughts and some intention of acting on them, but without a specific plan?
Ideation 5 (Specific plan and intent, recent): Have you worked out a method or plan for killing yourself, and do you intend to carry it out?
Ideation 1 (Wish to be dead, lifetime): Have you wished you were dead, or wished you could go to sleep and not wake up?
Ideation 2 (Nonspecific active thoughts, lifetime): Have you had thoughts of killing yourself, without thinking about a method, intent, or plan?
Ideation 3 (Method, without intent, lifetime): Have you thought about how you might kill yourself, without intending to act on those thoughts?
Ideation 4 (Some intent, no specific plan, lifetime): Have you had suicidal thoughts and some intention of acting on them, but without a specific plan?
Ideation 5 (Specific plan and intent, lifetime): Have you worked out a method or plan for killing yourself, and do you intend to carry it out?
Intensity, most severe recent ideation - Frequency: How often do the thoughts occur? (1=less than weekly, 2=once weekly, 3=2-5 days/week, 4=daily/almost daily, 5=many times daily)

Intensity, most severe recent ideation - Duration: When present, how long do they last? (1=seconds/minutes, 2=less than an hour, 3=1-4 hours, 4=4-8 hours/most of the day, 5=more than 8 hours or persistent)

Intensity, most severe recent ideation - Controllability: Can the person stop or control the thoughts? (0=does not try, 1=easily, 2=with little difficulty, 3=with some difficulty, 4=with much difficulty, 5=unable)

Intensity, most severe recent ideation - Deterrents: What has stopped the person from acting? (0=not applicable, 1=definitely stopped, 2=probably stopped, 3=uncertain, 4=probably did not stop, 5=definitely did not stop)

Intensity, most severe recent ideation - Reasons: Why does the person have the thoughts? (0=not applicable, 1=entirely attention/reaction, 2=mostly attention/reaction, 3=both equally, 4=mostly to end pain, 5=entirely to end pain)
Behavior (Actual suicide attempt, recent): Did the person engage in potentially self-injurious behavior with at least some intent to die? Injury is not required.
Behavior (Interrupted attempt, recent): Did another person or an outside circumstance stop the person after the attempt had begun but before the self-injurious act occurred?
Behavior (Aborted attempt, recent): Did the person begin steps toward an attempt but stop themselves before the self-injurious act occurred?
Behavior (Preparatory acts or behavior, recent): Did the person take steps toward an attempt, such as obtaining or arranging a method, writing a suicide note, or giving away possessions?
Behavior (Nonsuicidal self-injury, recent): Did the person intentionally injure themselves without suicidal intent? Document separately from suicidal behavior.
Behavior (Actual suicide attempt, lifetime): Did the person engage in potentially self-injurious behavior with at least some intent to die? Injury is not required.
Behavior (Interrupted attempt, lifetime): Did another person or an outside circumstance stop the person after the attempt had begun but before the self-injurious act occurred?
Behavior (Aborted attempt, lifetime): Did the person begin steps toward an attempt but stop themselves before the self-injurious act occurred?
Behavior (Preparatory acts or behavior, lifetime): Did the person take steps toward an attempt, such as obtaining or arranging a method, writing a suicide note, or giving away possessions?
Behavior (Nonsuicidal self-injury, lifetime): Did the person intentionally injure themselves without suicidal intent? Document separately from suicidal behavior.
Actual lethality/damage of the most recent actual attempt (recent), authorized form 0-5 coding. Record only when an actual attempt occurred in this window.
Potential lethality (recent), authorized form 0-2 coding. Record only when actual damage is 0.
Actual lethality/damage of the most recent actual attempt (lifetime), authorized form 0-5 coding. Record only when an actual attempt occurred in this window.
Potential lethality (lifetime), authorized form 0-2 coding. Record only when actual damage is 0.

source.note: Ideation levels 1-5, five intensity dimensions, five behavior categories, lethality codings, and demonstration triage flags.

assumptions: Ideation item wording below is a concise paraphrase of the source table; the authorized form governs exact administration wording and probes.
For each positive response the clinician documents timing, current-versus-historical status, the own description, and the determination, outside this structured payload.
A yes to a higher ideation level implies endorsement of lower levels clinically, but every level is still recorded explicitly here.
experimental_defaults: Form choice: full phenomenon coverage (ideation 1-5 in two windows, five intensity dimensions, five behavior categories in two windows, lethality codings); exact authorized wording is NOT reproduced.
Time windows: recent ideation = past_month, recent behavior = past_3_months, lifetime = lifetime.
No branching skips: all ideation levels are asked explicitly and a higher-level yes never fills in lower levels.
Intensity is rated for the most severe recent ideation and is required if and only if any recent ideation (levels 1-5) is endorsed.
Lethality codings are required if and only if an actual attempt occurred in that window; potential lethality additionally requires actual damage 0.
Nonsuicidal self-injury is documented separately: it contributes to clinical_review but never triggers high_risk_alert by itself.
Immediate emergency concern (current intent/plan, attempt in progress, inability to stay safe) is clinician-determined and is never a calculated flag.
source_gaps: The supplied source does not contain the authorized exact administration wording/probes; paraphrase status is preserved and must survive into S11.
Recency qualifiers in the source triage flags say typically past-month/past-3-month; fixed windows are the experimental choice.
The source gives no composite or cutoff beyond the demonstration triage flags; none is defined here.

validation_results.notes: Reference examples live in backend/tests/assessments/test_definitions.py (slice 3) and were worked independently from the source.

release.disclaimer: Experimental assessment package. Implementation validation replaces owner approval for this release; this does NOT establish clinical validation and introduces no treatment thresholds.
release.release_notes: Released for S11 C-SSRS implementation. No owner review or approval required or recorded.
